summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with severe psoriatic arthritis and multiple comorbidities was admitted for acute left leg and knee pain. He presented with a flare of his arthritis, including swelling and severe pain in the left knee, with radiating symptoms to the calf. Imaging ruled out fracture and DVT, and arthrocentesis revealed inflammatory fluid with no crystals or infection. Empiric antibiotics were started but discontinued after cultures remained negative. Prednisone was increased to 60 mg daily, resulting in significant improvement. He developed mild calf pain, which was monitored and attributed to inflammatory or neuropathic causes; gabapentin was initiated. A cervical trigger point injection was performed for headache, and he maintained good glycemic control on his insulin regimen. He was discharged home with a prednisone taper, continued immunosuppression, and follow-up arranged with rheumatology.
